chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) led us in the Dhuhr prayer, performing five ruku' (bowings). Then he turned away, and some of the people said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, has something been added to the prayer?' He said, 'What is that?' They said, 'You prayed with us five ruku'.' He said, so he faced the Qibla, said Takbir while sitting, then prostrated two prostrations, in which there was no recitation and no bowing, then he gave Salam, and he used to say, 'These are the two Prostrations of Dismissal (al-Murghimatayn).'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is a rare (shadh) report, not acted upon, because we have clarified that whoever adds to the prayer and knows it, it is obligatory upon him to restart the prayer. And if he doubts the addition, he prostrates the two Prostrations of Dismissal. It is permissible that the Imam (peace be upon him) did this because the statement of one person was not something decisive, and it is permissible that it was a mistake from him, and he prostrated the two prostrations out of precaution.

key_terms.الْمُرْغِمَتَانِ: The two Prostrations of Dismissal (specific term for prostrations due to doubt or addition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on adding an extra ruku' to the prayer and how are the two prostrations of dismissal performed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the Prophet’s (or Imam Ali’s) performance of five ruku' in Dhuhr, introducing the concept of 'al-Murghimatayn' (the two prostrations that silence the forgetful). Muhammad ibn al-Hasan clarifies its jurisprudential status as a *khabar shadh* (rare report), distinguishing between obligatory restart for known additions and precautionary prostrations for doubt, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ihtiyat* (precaution) in ritual purity.
